forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi participated in the Islamabad MOU process, with a final agreed text reached 12 June and the MOU digitally signed by named Iranian envoys on 14 June — before EOD 2026-06-16. This constitutes an official Iranian action rescinding the June 1 suspension per resolution criteria (signed state-level agreement by named principals = official rescinding of the suspension). Confirmed by TIER1: AP, Reuters, NPR, Vice President Vance announcement June 15. Ambiguity check: the June 14 signing is not merely a 'written-message exchange' but a formal bilateral agreement executed by Araghchi as named principal. Resolution: YES.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE: p 0.20 → 0.25. Post-Islamabad MOU (signed June 14-17), traffic surged: Kpler recorded ~20 tankers on June 19 (highest since June 2); CENTCOM reported 55 ships transiting June 20. However, Iran declared re-closure June 20 citing Israeli Lebanon actions — a disputed claim CENTCOM denied. Argus Media reported 'traffic unchanged' despite the surge claim. The 7-day rolling average remains well below 50 (pre-MOU: ~2-10/day; post-MOU peak: ~20-55 on specific days only). Demining has not commenced; Iran cannot guarantee safe passage under contested legal status. A 7-day average of 50+ by July 2 requires sustained, uncontested daily throughput for ~10 consecutive days — not yet established. Small uplift from MOU existence and June 19-20 surge; offset by re-closure dispute and unresolved mining.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE: p 0.30 → 0.55. Major uplift from three concurrent developments: (1) Islamabad MOU Point 4 mandates Iran 'make arrangements for safe passage' and demining to begin within 30 days of signing (i.e., by ~July 14-17, placing commencement before July 10 within the window); (2) UK/France multinational mine-clearing mission formally finalized post-MOU with 15 committed countries; (3) RFA Lyme Bay (with Royal Navy DTXG mine-hunting teams and autonomous minehunting systems) completed Mediterranean training and arrived in Cyprus, positioned for imminent forward deployment. Aspides designated as EU's primary demining role. Residual downside: Iran re-declared Hormuz closed June 20 citing Lebanon violations, which could delay the 'permissible environment' condition; and Iran has acknowledged difficulty locating some mines. Net assessment: MOU mandate + UK/France assets in position outweigh delay risk within the 18-day remaining window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: KEEP: p 0.45. No second or third reading of the dissolution bill has been confirmed as of June 22. The election date remains unresolved: Netanyahu wants October, Shas/UTJ want September before High Holy Days, and haredi-draft brinkmanship continues. The MOU/ceasefire context may reduce urgency for early elections (wartime-solidarity argument weakened by deal), but equally may accelerate the process if Netanyahu seeks a 'deal bonus' at the polls. The range Sept 8-Oct 20 remains the operative band; two readings remain. No material movement since June 10.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Bürgenstock High Level Committee produce a publicly shared nuclear framework document (covering enrichment levels and HEU disposal) by EOD 2026-07-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The June 21 Bürgenstock session established a High Level Committee with three working groups (nuclear, sanctions, monitoring/dispute). The Islamabad MOU gives 60 days (deadline ~mid-August) to finalize a deal; the nuclear file is the hardest (HEU disposal, enrichment cap unresolved). Historical precedent: JCPOA framework (April 2015) took ~3 months from open talks. P=0.30: 30-day sub-deadline for a nuclear framework document is ambitious; Iran's domestic politics (hardliner opposition) and the ongoing Lebanon/Hormuz disputes reduce the probability of a rapid nuclear text.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports that the Bürgenstock High Level Committee or its nuclear working group has produced and shared (publicly or via mediator read-out) a written framework document specifying proposed enrichment levels and/or HEU disposal modalities, before EOD 2026-07-22.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Iran International/Times of Israel, or a Pakistan/Qatar mediator joint statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Vague communiques or 'progress noted' statements without a specific written nuclear text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; public statements referencing 'agreement in principle' without a document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Iran formally suspend or block mine-countermeasure operations in Hormuz, citing Lebanon or ceasefire violations, before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast tracking the key downside risk to F5. Iran declared Hormuz closed June 20 (3 days after MOU signing) citing Israeli Lebanon violations — IRGC warned vessels against transiting in new radio messages. If Iran obstructs MCM vessel entry into the strait (militarily or legally), F5's YES resolution is blocked. P=0.35: Iran has strong incentive to use Hormuz access as leverage; the June 20 re-declaration demonstrates willingness to invoke ceasefire-violation language; but CENTCOM has shown it will enforce passage regardless of Iranian declarations.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran issues a TIER1-confirmed formal military order, official statement, or physical action (e.g., IRGC vessel interception or radio warning acted upon) that delays or halts the entry or operation of MCM assets in the Strait of Hormuz, before EOD 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/CNBC/CNN or a named CENTCOM/UK MoD/coalition statement confirming Iranian obstruction; IRGC statement alone is insufficient without corroboration.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Rhetorical re-closure declarations without physical enforcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; IRGC radio warnings not acted upon = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; delays due to logistics only (not Iranian action) = RESOLVE-NO.
